papers.title: An open-set learning framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage open-set learning framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification that uses an adaptive Gaussian method with quantile-based adaptive thresholds to model known sleep categories and a trainable decision boundary OpenMax module to refine classification. On three public EEG datasets, the method achieved strong known-stage classification while effectively detecting unknown sleep categories, significantly improving open-set recognition performance.

papers.title: An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization.
papers.journal: Digest of technical papers. Symposium on VLSI Technology
papers.summary: The work presents a 65 nm system-on-chip for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation that performs low-noise in-ear EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A dedicated accelerator with long-kernel memory reuse and runtime dynamic quantization reduced model size by 3.88× with only 0.28% accuracy loss, achieving 98.3% sensitivity for deep sleep detection.

papers.title: Atlas-Based Electrical Source Imaging for Mouse EEG: Application to an Fmr1 Knockout Model.
papers.summary: The study built an atlas-based electrical source imaging pipeline for 30-channel mouse EEG and tested it against simulated dipoles, finding that a region-of-interest source space with an ellipsoid head model and sLORETA recovered superficial sources to a mean error of 0.93 mm. Applied to resting EEG from Fmr1 knockout and wild-type mice, gamma power was elevated in knockouts and localized to six parcels, with relative power in Delta, Theta, and High Gamma and both aperiodic parameters varying by region.

papers.title: When More Is Not Better: Component Anti-Synergy in a P300 Speller
papers.summary: The paper tested whether combining individually promising components in a P300 speller is additive using a four-component full-factorial experiment varying Euclidean Alignment, xDAWN spatial filtering, subject calibration, and language model priors on a public dataset. Results showed that component value is conditional rather than additive, with calibration the strongest singular contributor, anti-synergy between components, and language model support not universally beneficial.

papers.title: pyAvalanches: A Python Package for Analyzing Spatiotemporal Propagation in Neuronal Avalanches
papers.summary: The paper introduces pyAvalanches, an open-source Python package providing a standardized end-to-end pipeline for neuronal avalanche analysis from electrophysiological recordings, with core innovation in computing Avalanche Transition Matrices to map spatiotemporal propagation patterns and derive network-based metrics. It demonstrates utility through group-level analysis of a public resting-state EEG dataset comparing propagation patterns across clinical populations.

papers.title: Seasonal variations in the polysomnographic sleep/wake cycle and activity/rest pattern in the dromedary camel (Camelus dromedarius).
papers.journal: Journal of comparative physiology. B, Biochemical, systemic, and environmental physiology
papers.summary: The study investigated seasonal variations in sleep/wake cycle and activity/rest patterns of captive dromedary camels using polysomnography and behavioral observations across four seasons. Key findings showed that in winter, total sleep time was significantly higher (4.8 h) compared to summer (3.6 h), and wakefulness percentage was lower in winter (52.9%) than summer (59.8%), with activity duration decreasing from 17.1 h in summer to 11.6 h in winter.

papers.title: Brain network dynamics in the wake-sleep transition reorganize according to task engagement.
papers.summary: Used simultaneous EEG-fMRI to examine brain network dynamics during the wake-sleep transition in humans performing either an active or passive auditory task. Found that decreasing alertness led to increased parietal synchronization during passive listening, but active task engagement recruited long-range frontoparietal synchronization and auditory cortex synchronization while thalamocortical synchronization increased only during passive listening.

papers.title: Reduced dynamical variability in depression: evidence from EEG and QIF-E network simulation.
authors: Thaise Graziele L de O Toutain
papers.summary: The study compared EEG complexity in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) patients and healthy controls using multiscale entropy (MSE), finding higher mean entropy at broader time scales and reduced inter-individual variability in MDD. Simulations with a Quadratic Integrate-and-Fire network showed that configurations lacking local electrical coupling reproduced key MDD entropy features, suggesting that local coupling structure modulates complexity-variability balance.

papers.title: Distinct oscillatory neural rhythms support representational precision and confidence in working memory.
papers.summary: Using EEG combined with a spatial working memory task requiring trial-by-trial uncertainty reports, the study found that alpha-band activity encodes memory content with precision predicting uncertainty reports, while beta-band activity carries a scalar confidence signal with slow dynamics. These results demonstrate that representational precision and scalar confidence are multiplexed across distinct oscillatory rhythms.

papers.title: Clinical utility of in-ear EEG electrodes in hospitalized patients: comparison with standard scalp EEG.
papers.summary: The study evaluated in-ear EEG against standard scalp EEG in 30 hospitalized patients, finding 83.3% sensitivity, 80.0% specificity, and 82.8% accuracy for detecting neurophysiological abnormalities, with substantial agreement for encephalopathy grading. In-ear EEG was well-suited for diffuse dysfunction but missed one focal seizure, indicating reduced spatial coverage.

papers.title: Interictal electric source imaging with open-source software and routine low-density electroencephalography: A systematic comparison of four inverse methods in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.summary: The study assessed interictal electrical source imaging (ESI) diagnostic accuracy using open-source software and low-density EEG with four inverse methods in drug-resistant epilepsy patients. sLORETA at the half-rising phase achieved the highest performance (accuracy 81.0%, sensitivity 82.5%, specificity 77.3%) and significantly outperformed minimum norm, with robust results across challenging subgroups.

papers.title: Time-frequency EEG markers of word boundaries in speech production.
papers.summary: The EEG study used time-frequency analysis to compare word-boundary and within-word syllable transitions during pseudoword production, revealing differential recruitment of left and right inferior frontal and left superior temporal sources. Word transitions showed elevated theta and beta synchronization in right inferior frontal cortex, while alpha suppression in left superior temporal lobe suggested increased sensory prediction at word onset.

papers.title: Interpretable AI for neural signal decoding in dementia: an EEG ensemble approach to differential diagnosis.
papers.summary: The study developed an interpretable ensemble machine learning framework using EEG features from resting-state and photic stimulation to differentiate Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia, achieving 95.63% accuracy on a held-out test set. SHAP analysis identified beta-band hemispheric asymmetry and alpha-band reactivity as key discriminative features.

papers.title: Large-scale neuromorphic modeling of cortical networks on FPGA for investigating anesthetic-induced neural dynamics.
papers.summary: This paper presents a high-performance FPGA-based neuromorphic hardware implementation of a cortical network comprising 10,000 spiking neurons using the Izhikevich model to investigate anesthetic-induced neural dynamics. The system achieves real-time simulation and demonstrates that adjusting synaptic weights and network parameters can continuously monitor state transitions in neural synchronization and firing patterns relevant to general anesthesia.

papers.title: Distinct roles of brain network flexibility in motor learning across age.
papers.summary: EEG study of younger and older adults during a visuomotor learning task found that the learning aftereffect was associated with brain network flexibility during motor preparation in younger adults, but this association was absent in older adults.

papers.title: Talking Brains: Neonatal Aperiodic Activity in Resting State EEG Relates to Later Communicative Abilities
papers.summary: This study examined whether aperiodic activity in neonatal resting-state EEG relates to communicative abilities at 12 months in 50 typically developing infants, extracting aperiodic offset and exponent using the FOOOF algorithm. Quadratic regression showed an inverted U-shaped relationship between the neonatal aperiodic exponent and later communicative abilities, with both lower and higher exponent values associated with poorer outcomes and intermediate values with better abilities.

papers.title: EEG resting-state gamma power as a potential biomarker of excitation / inhibition imbalance in autism: Evidence from the Autism Biomarkers Consortium for Clinical Trials.
papers.journal: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology
papers.summary: Analysis of resting-state EEG from 399 autistic children and typically developing peers across four timepoints found increased gamma power in autistic children, which was longitudinally associated with lower non-verbal IQ and memory for faces.

papers.title: Bio-inspired Terrain Perception for Snake Robots: Spectral Analysis of Vertical Undulation and Sidewinding.
papers.summary: Inspired by biological snake mechanosensation, this study proposes a proprioceptive terrain classification framework for snake robots using a single uniaxial accelerometer and a Band-Limited Spectral Magnitude feature. Validated on concrete, gravel, grass, and sand across vertical undulation and sidewinding, a hierarchical strategy achieved classification accuracies exceeding 98.8% for vertical undulation and up to 92.5% for sidewinding, with optimal frequency bands aligning with biological snake mechanoreceptor sensitivity.

papers.title: A Generalizable OPM-MEG Framework for Time-resolved Language Decoding During Natural Speech Production.
papers.summary: OPM-MEG and EEG were compared during overt speech production in Mandarin speakers; OPM-MEG showed higher decoding accuracy for vowel rhymes, with CSP and Linear SVM yielding the best performance and significant OPM-MEG > EEG differences at 150-500 ms.

papers.title: Salience network orchestrates large-scale brain dynamics during target detection: Insights from an EEG dFNC study.
papers.summary: EEG dynamic functional network connectivity during a visual oddball task revealed a filtering-integration-regulation framework, with salience network engagement strength predicting P300 amplitude and its timing predicting P300 latency.

papers.title: Multivariate decoding of EEG reveals key spatial and temporal distinctions in perception and valuation.
papers.summary: Multivariate decoding of EEG during a multi-attribute decision-making task showed that perceptual representations emerged early and in parallel, attribute value decoding emerged sequentially, and integrated value representations preceded amplification of perceptual representations.

papers.title: Bidirectional EEG Neurofeedback of Sensorimotor Beta Oscillations Reveals Asymmetric Modulation and Strategy-Dependent Learning.
papers.summary: This exploratory double-blind sham-controlled within-subjects study tested whether 15 healthy participants could bidirectionally modulate sensorimotor beta power over C3 using EEG neurofeedback and examined learning trends. Thirteen participants successfully decreased beta activity, three successfully increased it, and two showed bidirectional control; real ENF success was significantly higher than sham only when sham was received first, indicating a transfer learning effect and strategy-dependent rather than stable plasticity.

papers.title: EEG signatures for tactile object individuation on a finger tip.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
papers.summary: EEG study of tactile object individuation found that neural activity around 860 ms encoded pin numerosity only during enumeration, with N1000cc, tCDA, and alpha-band activity indexing capacity-limited tactile object individuation.

papers.title: Retrieval practice prevents stress-induced inference impairment and preserves rapid bridge-related memory reactivation
papers.summary: Acute stress impaired A-C inference accuracy and speed and disrupted rapid EEG reactivation of bridge element B, while retrieval practice buffered these stress effects and enhanced bridge reactivation beyond the non-stress condition.

papers.title: Neuronal Regulation and Locomotion in Rats Following Spinal Cord Injury: Reconciling Behavioral Scales With Neuroelectrophysiology.
papers.summary: This perspective evaluates the discrepancy between behavioral recovery metrics (e.g., BBB scale) and neuroelectrophysiological outcomes (MEPs/SSEPs) in rodent spinal cord injury models. It argues that relying solely on locomotor scales overestimates functional tract integrity and advocates for integrating synchronized behavioral and electrophysiological profiling to improve predictive validity in preclinical trials.

papers.title: Serial amplitude-integrated electroencephalography trajectories and brain-injury-associated functional immaturity in extremely preterm infants.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study characterized postmenstrual-age-specific Burdjalov maturation trajectories using serial amplitude-integrated EEG in 156 extremely preterm infants, comparing those with and without major brain injury. Infants with brain injury had persistently lower Burdjalov scores (e.g., 1.45 points lower at PMA 32 weeks), but the linear interaction was unstable and not reproduced by ordinal models, cautioning against interpreting it as biological recovery.

papers.title: EEG markers of cholinergic dysfunction in Lewy body diseases: A review.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes EEG findings in Lewy body diseases and identifies reduced alpha reactivity, dominant frequency slowing, altered band power, and higher-frequency functional connectivity as promising non-invasive markers of cholinergic dysfunction.

papers.title: Reduced Motor Preparation and Altered EEG Signatures of Prediction in Autistic Adults.
papers.summary: Autistic adults showed less behavioral benefit from high-probability cues and reduced late CNV, altered mu/beta desynchronization, and weaker 1 Hz neural entrainment, implicating reduced motor preparation and altered prediction in autism.

papers.title: EEG-Based Auditory Attention Recognition Using DSCANet: An Innovative Incremental Learning Framework.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper proposes DSCANet, an incremental learning framework for EEG-based auditory attention recognition that integrates a Dynamic Self-Organizing Convolutional Attention Network with Elastic Weight Consolidation. Under 1-second decision windows in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, DSCANet achieved 81.51% accuracy on KUL and 63.03% on DTU, exceeding the strongest baseline by 3.41 and 6.23 percentage points, while showing improved stability against catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Tai Chi modulates resting alpha and theta EEG rhythms in female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence during compulsory detoxification.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial examined EEG alpha and theta rhythm modulation following a 6-month Tai Chi intervention versus routine physical rehabilitation in 32 female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence. Both groups showed reduced resting alpha and theta power after the intervention, while an acute bout of Tai Chi elicited higher alpha and theta power compared to treadmill exercise, suggesting distinct cortical relaxation effects.

papers.title: Modulation of fronto-parietal and autonomic activity underpins preserved working memory in middle-aged adults.
papers.summary: This study compared middle-aged high and low performers on a visuo-spatial working memory task to young adults using EEG and pupillometry. High-performing middle-aged adults exhibited prompt pupil dilation and distinct parietal alpha/beta and frontal theta event-related desynchronization during encoding and retention, suggesting that preserved working memory in midlife relies on flexible modulation of autonomic and cortical resources.

papers.title: Endovascular Electroencephalography at the Threshold of Clinical Translation: From Epilepsy Monitoring to a Broader Neural Interface.
papers.summary: This letter discusses endovascular electroencephalography as it approaches clinical translation, from epilepsy monitoring toward broader neural interface applications.

papers.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Studied differential privacy (DP) for clinical EEG feature anonymization using Gaussian and Laplace perturbations across client-side, centralized, and decentralized deployment scenarios. Found that the choice of mechanism, privacy parameters, and sensitivity calibration strongly influenced data utility, highlighting a practical privacy-utility trade-off in small, imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

papers.title: Emotional responses to naturalistic and artificial intelligence (AI)-generated affective pictures: A systematic comparison.
papers.summary: The study compared emotional responses to AI-generated and naturalistic affective pictures by recording pupil diameter, EEG, and self-reported valence and arousal from 109 participants. Emotionally charged pictures elicited stronger responses than neutral ones for both picture types, but with weaker effect sizes for AI-generated pictures; ratings and EEG measures were strongly correlated between matched AI and original pictures.

papers.title: Heartfulness Meditation-induced State and Trait Effects on Long-term, Short-term and Non-meditators Using Connectivity Analysis: An EEG Study on Prefrontal Cortex.
papers.summary: Assessed Heartfulness meditation's state and trait effects on prefrontal EEG connectivity and graph-theoretic measures in long-term meditators, short-term meditators, and non-meditators across baseline, meditation, transmission, and post-transmission states. Found improved coordination, increased global and local efficiency (state effect), and significant trait changes in long-term meditators in delta, theta, and alpha bands.

papers.title: Neural correlates of response inhibition following cognitive behavioral therapy in obsessive-compulsive disorder: a randomized controlled EEG study.
papers.summary: Randomized controlled trial examining whether 12-week CBT with exposure and response prevention alters behavioral and electrophysiological indices of response inhibition in 60 adults with OCD. Found that CBT significantly reduced OCD symptom severity, increased No-Go P3 amplitude (Group × Time interaction), and reduced commission errors compared to a waitlist control.

papers.title: PQ-Neurolink: latency-aware post-quantum-ready secure communication for distributed brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: PQ-NeuroLink is a latency-aware post-quantum-ready communication framework that separates authenticated session establishment from symmetric streaming for distributed EEG brain-computer interfaces. In the constrained BLE 1-hop condition, hybrid ML-KEM-768 plus X25519 mode increased p95 latency by only 0.45 ms relative to the unsecured baseline while maintaining 99.0% packet delivery.

papers.title: Network integration of neocortical Cajal-Retzius neurons shapes early cortical dynamics and contributes to their transient nature.
papers.summary: Using immunohistochemistry, three-dimensional reconstruction, electrophysiology, calcium imaging, multiplexed FISH, and optogenetics, this study shows that neocortical Cajal-Retzius neurons receive dense GABAergic inputs, are spontaneously active and synchronized with network activity, and maintain an NKCC1-dominant chloride transporter profile. Chronic optogenetic activation accelerated Cajal-Retzius neuron loss, and NKCC1 blockade reduced their loss in vitro, indicating their activity contributes to their transient nature.

papers.title: A Systematic Review of fNIRS-Based Neurovascular Coupling Research: Methodological Landscape and Translational Considerations for Spaceflight.
papers.summary: Systematic review of 66 fNIRS-based neurovascular coupling studies in healthy adults (2015–2025), summarizing methodological approaches and physiological findings to assess translational potential for spaceflight. Found that most studies used cognitive paradigms, multimodal designs, and single stressors (e.g., hypoxia, sleep deprivation), with no studies combining stressors or validating spaceflight conditions, concluding that current evidence does not support fNIRS-based NVC monitoring for space missions.

papers.title: Acute catatonia and psychosis in the context of seizure exacerbation in epilepsy: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 44-year-old woman with epilepsy who developed acute catatonia and psychosis after switching from clomipramine to venlafaxine and experiencing increased seizure frequency. Management with benzodiazepines and cautious antipsychotic uptitration (quetiapine XR, cariprazine) led to complete catatonic and psychotic symptom remission over 29 days, highlighting diagnostic uncertainty, pharmacokinetic interactions, and cardiac safety considerations.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
